## What's new

**Website tunnels go through a real reverse proxy.** warren now reads each
request instead of passing the bytes through untouched, which brings:

- `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Host` and `X-Forwarded-Proto`, so your app
  sees the visitor's IP and whether they used `https`. Any of these headers
  a visitor makes up are dropped.
- **Password protection:** `warren http 3000 --auth me:a-long-password`.
  The password protects the tunnel; your app never sees it.
- **IP allowlists:** `warren http 3000 --allow 203.0.113.7,198.51.100.0/24`.
- **Request logs** in your warren window, one line per request:
  `GET  200  12ms  81.2.69.160  /index.html`.
- HTTP/2 for visitors on `https://`. WebSockets keep working.

**HTTPS for website tunnels without a wildcard certificate.** Add
`"https_addr": ":443"` and `"acme": true` to `server.json`, and every website
tunnel gets its own Let's Encrypt certificate as it opens. It works with any
DNS provider and needs no certbot. Port 443 must be reachable from the
internet. Re-running `setup.sh` offers this too. See "HTTPS website tunnels
without a wildcard" in the install guide, including Let's Encrypt's limit of
50 certificates a week (random subdomains each need a new one).

**Faster connections.** Clients keep a few connections to the server open
ahead of time, so a new player or visitor no longer waits for a fresh
handshake.

**New server options** for website tunnels:

- `"https_redirect": true` sends `http://` visitors to `https://`.
- `"trusted_proxies": ["127.0.0.1"]` for nginx (or another proxy) in front of
  warren, so visitor IPs and `--allow` are right. **If nginx sits in front of
  your warren, add this**, or re-run `setup.sh`, which adds it and the
  matching nginx headers.
- `"log_requests": true` logs every website request in the server log.

## Updating

Clients and servers from 0.5.0 and 0.6.0 work together in any combination,
so nobody has to update at the same time. Older versions simply don't use
the new features. The one exception is on purpose: `--auth` and `--allow`
need a 0.6.0 server. Against an older server, warren refuses to start rather
than put the site online unprotected.

- On website tunnels, `max_conns_per_tunnel` now counts requests in progress
  (including open WebSockets) rather than connections.
- If you turn on `"acme": true`, don't downgrade the server afterwards: older
  versions don't know the option and would serve plain HTTP on port 443.
- Building from source now needs Go 1.26 or newer, and warren has its first
  dependency (`golang.org/x/crypto`, for the certificates). The downloads
  below are still single files with nothing else to install.

The Minecraft mod hasn't changed (still 0.2.0); it's included so everything
is in one place.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `warren-windows-amd64.exe` | Windows |
| `warren-darwin-arm64` | Mac with Apple chip (M1–M4) |
| `warren-darwin-amd64` | Mac with Intel chip |
| `warren-linux-amd64` | Linux / most VPSes |
| `warren-linux-arm64` | Linux on ARM (Oracle Ampere, Hetzner ARM, Raspberry Pi 64-bit) |
| `warren-mod-0.2.0+mc1.21.11.jar` | Minecraft mod (Fabric 1.21.11, needs Fabric API) |
| `setup.sh` | VPS setup wizard |
| `SHA256SUMS` | checksums (also used by `warren update`) |
